title: HB70 (2021 Regular): AN ACT relating to firearms.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Kentucky); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Kentucky text (Introduced, 0000-00-00; official copy, https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/21RS/hb70/orig_bill.pdf (LegiScan doc 2228689))
provenance.note: As-filed text (21 RS BR 202); no passage vote and later amendments are not in the text read. Quotes join separate sub-parts with one space and skip some items in Section 2(1)(a) (2. to 4.) for length. Section 12(2) (not quoted in full) bars renting, selling, transferring or offering a firearm to a person known to be found dangerous. Section 13 (KRS 16.220) amends firearm disposal; the Administrative Office of the Courts statistics duty is in Section 11.

operative_text:
Section 2 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (1) A District Court may issue a warrant to search for and seize a firearm in the possession of a respondent who is dangerous if: (a) A law enforcement officer provides the court a sworn affidavit that: 1. States why the law enforcement officer believes the respondent is dangerous and in possession of a firearm; (b) The District Court determines that probable cause exists to believe that the respondent is: 1. Dangerous; and 2. In possession of a firearm.
Section 3 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (1) If a law enforcement officer seizes a firearm from a respondent whom the law enforcement officer believes to be dangerous without obtaining a warrant, the law enforcement officer shall submit to a District Court having jurisdiction over the respondent an affidavit describing the basis for the law enforcement officer's belief that the respondent is dangerous.
Section 4 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (2) The Commonwealth has the burden of proving all material facts by clear and convincing evidence.
Section 4 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (6) If the court determines that the Commonwealth has proved by clear and convincing evidence that the respondent is dangerous, the court shall issue a written order: (a) Finding the respondent is dangerous; (b) Ordering the law enforcement agency having custody of the seized firearm to retain the firearm; (c) Ordering the respondent's license to carry a concealed firearm, if applicable, suspended; and (d) Enjoining the respondent from: 1. Renting; 2. Receiving transfer of; 3. Owning; or 4. Possessing; a firearm.
Section 6 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (1) At least one hundred eighty (180) days after the date on which a District Court ordered a law enforcement agency to retain a respondent's firearm under Section 4 of this Act, the respondent may petition the District Court for a finding that he or she is no longer dangerous.
Section 12 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (1) No person who has been found to be dangerous by a District Court having jurisdiction over the person following a hearing under Section 4 of this Act shall knowingly or intentionally: (a) Rent; (b) Purchase; (c) Receive transfer of; (d) Own; or (e) Possess; a firearm.
Section 12 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (3) Any person who violates subsection (1) of this section is guilty of a Class A misdemeanor.
Section 12 (new section of KRS Chapter 237): (4) Any person who violates subsection (2) of this section is guilty of a Class D felony.
